subject: Cognitive Science
title: Schemas and Scripts
description: A fast breakdown of Schemas and Scripts for builders.

hook.text: You walk into a restaurant and know to wait for a table, order from a menu, and tip. Nobody taught you the steps.

buildup.text: Roger Schank called these scripts—pre-written sequences your brain runs in familiar situations.

discovery.text: Schemas are broader: they organize objects, roles, and expectations into reusable mental packages.

twist.text: Scripts can mislead. In a foreign country, your restaurant script may be completely wrong.

climax.text: When scripts break, you feel confused and slow—proof of how much thinking they normally handle.

punchline.text: Your brain scripts the familiar so you can think about the new.

quiz.question: What is a cognitive script?
options: A pre-written mental sequence for familiar situations
